oct12.summary: Robert Yard, under-secretary, to the Earl of Manchester, ambassador in Paris: messengers wait at Dover for Mills; the Lords Justices of Ireland report disaffected persons returning and an ill design against the government, with like intimations from Scotland, all said to be carried on very privately at Saint-Germain; a letter from Lebrun at Paris enclosing one for a Mr Gray was opened at the post house.

oct16.summary: Mills has gone by way of Rouen, so warrants are out and three messengers watch the coast, London and Dover for him and Lord Drummond's priest; directions on Fowles; no goldsmith Cockburne in Round Court; Clance the periwig maker has gone to France and should be watched.

snip.cap: Yard to Manchester, Whitehall, 12 October 1699, p. 1: runs of figure groups set inside the clear English
